title: Crispy Blanched Brussels Sprouts (Oven or Air Fryer)
subtitle: 5-minute blanch · 2-minute steam-dry · two crispy finishing methods
headnote: DRAFT / UNTESTED — Adapted from the YouTube video “I Found a Better Way to Roast Brussels Sprouts” by ThatDudeCanCook. The defining technique is to blanch halved Brussels sprouts for 5 minutes in salted water, let them steam-dry for 2 minutes, toss with olive oil and a little more salt, then roast or air-fry until crisp outside and creamy inside. The presenter did not specify the sprouts weight or exact oil amount; quantities below are editorial starting estimates and have not been tested.

ingredientGroups.title: Brussels sprouts and blanching water
items: 680 g Brussels sprouts (editorial starting estimate; amount not stated in video)
1 heaping tablespoon sea salt for blanching water (exact weight depends on salt; video amount)

ingredientGroups.title: Seasoning before finishing
items: About 25–35 g olive oil, enough to coat evenly (editorial estimate; video says a generous amount)
A little additional sea salt, less than 1 teaspoon as described in video (adjust to taste)

steps: Trim the dry stem end off each Brussels sprout. Remove any damaged outer leaves and cut each sprout in half lengthwise.
Bring 3.8 L (4 quarts) water to a boil. Add 1 heaping tablespoon sea salt. Carefully add the halved Brussels sprouts and boil for 5 minutes.
Drain thoroughly and allow the sprouts to steam-dry in the colander for approximately 2 minutes. Surface moisture should dissipate before roasting.
Transfer sprouts to a bowl. Toss with enough olive oil to coat and a small extra sprinkle of salt (less than 1 tsp, according to the video).

OVEN METHOD: Heat a convection oven to 400°F. Arrange the sprouts cut-side down on a rimmed sheet pan in a single layer. Roast about 20 minutes, until deeply browned and crisp at the cut faces. Start checking early; ovens vary.

AIR-FRYER METHOD: Preheat the air fryer to 430°F (only if the appliance supports this setting). Arrange in an uncrowded single layer, cut-side up. Air-fry about 15 minutes, checking during the final minutes for deep browning and crisp edges. Cook in batches if needed.
Serve immediately while the outer leaves are crunchy and the centers are tender and creamy. Taste and adjust salt.
notes: Use one finishing method, not both. The oven method gives particularly deep cut-side browning from contact with the hot sheet pan; the air fryer is convenient when oven space is limited.
Do not crowd the sheet pan or air fryer basket: overcrowding traps steam and limits crisping.
The video's air-fryer setting is 430°F; check your machine's maximum setting. If it tops out at 400°F, do not assume the same 15-minute timing.
Optional glazes are discussed but not included in the base recipe. The speaker mentions a separate sherry-maple glaze video without providing its recipe.
